concrete_requests: Report the sum of sensor readings over the run, and how many steps fall below 0.05 (line-loss steps).
Report max_error and the step at which the first line loss occurs on each track.
Report whether the signal stays inside the sensor weight range (±2) or saturates on the s-bend and slalom.
Report completion_time and completion for the oval, if any run finishes.
questions: Does the wider ±0.06 m span keep max_error below the 0.06 m off-track limit?
Does the 16 mm footprint with 0.02 m spacing give a smooth signal, or does the noise increase at the centre?
Does mass 0.6 kg reduce steering oscillation without causing overshoot?
Which single geometry change would most reduce line_loss_events on the slalom?

intent: Test whether a wider seven-sensor span (±0.06 m) with larger 16 mm footprints keeps the line in view at the offsets where iteration 0 lost it, and whether a lighter body (0.6 kg) corrects faster. Expected result: at least one completed run on the oval and far fewer off-track ends, with max_error below 0.06 m. If line losses persist, the next step is to widen the span further or move the row forward.
learning: Iteration 0 showed that the failure is an off-track drift that begins after the line is lost near ±0.05 m. The off-track limit is fixed at 0.06 m for any body width in range, so sensing is the lever. This iteration tests whether a wider span and larger footprints address that.
rationale: Iteration 0 failed on every track: all 60 trials went off track, with about one line-loss event each and progress of only 0.09 to 0.21. The max_error of about 0.063 m is above the 0.06 m off-track limit, so the robot drifts off just after it loses the line. Body width cannot widen that limit: max(0.06, 0.0125 + bw/4) stays at 0.06 for any bw up to 0.18. The fix therefore has to come from sensing. The ±0.04 m span loses the tape at about the same lateral offset where the run ends, so the controller gets no graded signal in time. I widen the span to ±0.06 m with seven sensors at 0.02 m spacing. I also enlarge the sensor footprint to 0.016 m. A 16 mm footprint at 0.03 m spacing leaves gaps of about 14 mm, which is smaller than the 25 mm tape, so at least one sensor always sees tape while the line is inside the span. Mass drops from 0.8 to 0.6 kg to cut yaw inertia so the body can correct faster. Wheel track, wheel radius and body dimensions stay as they were, because the evidence points at tracking error, not speed. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, max_error held below 0.06 m, and completion on the oval. The main risk is that the wider span adds signal noise near the centre, so the Integrator may need a lower kp.
